about: What SLATE can do, one capability a row, each held to the code by tools/capabilities.mjs: every command, look, route and file it names must exist, and every command a player issues must be named by a live row. Status is one of Missing, Partial, Implemented, Verified, Blocked, Retired. Verified means a test the gate runs (tests/**/*.test.ts) drives every command the row names through the engine (sim.execute, or run as a screen issues it) and checks the outcome and the readers the row claims, the standard docs/GAMEPLAY-COVERAGE.md holds a verified row to. A test that sets the change or a reader’s input by hand, calls a function in place of the command, or calls a reader the clock calls on its own (the day’s draw, the idle check, the month’s end) in the clock’s place or with its draw given, checks less: where a claimed outcome or reader is checked only that way, or not at all, the row isn’t Verified, or its claim is narrowed to what’s tested, and limits says which. A precondition set by hand (wages typed in, a document put in), a purchase made through the engine’s own spend, and a reader’s figure read by calling it after the command are setup, where the command and what reads it still run through the engine, and limits says so. Until a fourth review on 2026-10-12 this said any function called directly checked less, while docs/GAMEPLAY-COVERAGE.md counted those last two as setup, so a row could pass one standard and owe a note under the other. A check in the app or a tool outside the gate (manual, tools/acceptance-ui.mjs) can support a row and can’t make it Verified. Implemented means code exists for all of it and no such test checks one or more of its outcomes or claimed readers, which limits names, its verified layer Partial, or Missing where nothing in the gate checks it at all. Partial means the capability can’t be fully reached in a New Haven student’s life, and limits says why; a command out of reach and tested only on a life set up elsewhere is said so, as docs/GAMEPLAY-COVERAGE.md calls such a command unresolved. A command a New Haven life reaches, tested on a life no new one lives (a New Yorker’s, a Londoner’s), can still be Verified, and limits says on what life. The four layers are kept apart: a field in the model (schema) is not content, content is not a working interaction, and an interaction is not verified behavior. The rows of the brief of 2026-10-08 (the career, the industry, its database and the rail) are Retired, kept as the record of what was built. The connected world of 2026-10-09 added a row for every capability of the current world, the denominator being those rows, and said they named all of its commands. Nothing checked that, and it wasn’t so: on 2026-10-12, 139 of the 248 kinds the inventory then listed were in no live row, 43 of them commands a player issues and 96 the engine’s own (scheduled kinds, passage reactors and events, which no player issues). That day added the rows that name those 43 and the four the inventory hadn’t caught up with (brief.reader, work.identify, work.try, work.settle), and the tool’s check that every kind registered with onCommand, the inventory’s Commands, is named by one. Later that day a review held the rows to the standard docs/GAMEPLAY-COVERAGE.md is held to: coursework, how-you-play, practice-and-genres and practice-briefs, called Verified until then, each named a command whose outcome no test drove and checked, and each is Implemented, its limits saying what’s driven and what isn’t. A second review the same day found more of the same: accounts-and-transfers, credit-card, passport-and-id, classmates, production-rehearsal, cabaret and social-security-number, called Verified until then, each claimed a reader or an outcome no test checked, and each is Implemented; borrowing, called Verified, named bank.arrange_overdraft, which no American bank offers, and is Partial; and kept-context was Verified on tools/rail-check.mjs alone, which clicked a Career gone since 2026-10-09, so it’s Implemented with nothing in the gate checking it, and the tool no longer takes a check in the app alone as Verified. A third review the same day found more. Six rows called Verified until then (look-after-yourself, sleep, partner-rehearsals, doctor-and-appointments, cash and plays-to-read) each claimed a reader or an outcome no test drove and checked, and account-upkeep reached an account’s dormancy only by calling its handler with the idle time typed in: each is Implemented. Three named a reader their tests didn’t reach, and stay Verified on what the tests do check, with that reader out of the claim: what-needs-you named requireDecision as reading a dismissal to stop asking, which it doesn’t; term-deposits, the networth look, which no test checks a term in; and card-offers, allocatePayment, tested only as a function with the plan set by hand. The reason residence-and-citizenship gave for Partial, that reaching it needed income after the degree, was false: a wealthy or inherited New Haven student meets Mexico’s savings test on the first day. The four Verified rows whose commands came after docs/GAMEPLAY-COVERAGE.md’s audit of 2026-10-10 (tax-return’s tax.pay_state and tax.amend, leave-and-withdrawal, school-balance-and-aid and tax-payment-plans) were read against the standard by opening their tests: they hold, and each says now what’s set by hand and on what life. From then the tool also fails a Verified row whose cited tests don’t issue each of its commands, by its kind or the constant that holds it. A fourth review the same day found the two registries disagreeing on commands both named, and tools/coverage.mjs, which said so, outside the gate. plans-and-the-clock, what-needs-you, orientation-and-classes, term-deposits, payments, card-security, health-cover and tax-payment-plans, called Verified until then, each named a command docs/GAMEPLAY-COVERAGE.md calls partial, a claimed outcome or reader no test reaches through the engine, and each is Implemented, its limits naming the gap; what-needs-you and term-deposits, kept Verified by the third review with a reader each out of the claim, still claimed one their tests don’t reach (prune and the action’s refusal of a decision dismissed; a term’s maturity after its interest is taken). opt, Partial, said Verified in its verified layer. production-rehearsal called school.learn_part checked on a night factor its own limits said mixes it with the rest, another-bank called bank.set_order_source checked, and borrowing said paying collections was driven, each a command docs/GAMEPLAY-COVERAGE.md calls partial; and the limits of other rows didn’t name commands it calls partial or unresolved. plans-and-the-clock also said the clock ran fast and faster, which the command refuses. From then tools/capabilities.mjs, which the gate runs, holds the agreement on every command both name: a Verified row has every row of its commands there verified and read, a command unresolved there sits in a Partial row, a command partial or unresolved there is named in a sentence of the row’s limits that gives that word (or out of reach, for one unresolved), and a verified layer says Verified only on a Verified row. What limits says of a command is still held by reading. A check of that settlement the same day found two more rows Verified on a reader no test reaches through the command: school-money, an elective shift’s payday and the wages it records for the return, and working-it-through, a night played after a way is kept on a part; each is Implemented. It also found the agreement reading a command’s actions as the command: look-after-yourself’s limits named life.look_after:order partial, and that sentence passed for the wash, the workout and the hour unwound, which docs/GAMEPLAY-COVERAGE.md called partial too, while the same limits called a shower and an hour unwinding checked through the command. From then a row of one of a command’s actions is named in limits by its own id (life.look_after:wash), with its word.

Driven through life.sleep and checked: the clock moves by exactly the hours asked, across a clock change too; energy comes back and sleep debt is paid down, or grows on a short night; the night’s quality is read at the hour it starts; the waking day is charged from the wake; and the world goes on while they sleep (tests/simulation.test.ts, tests/looks.test.ts, tests/personality.test.ts, tests/wellbeing-bites.test.ts). It’s refused while the guide holds it (tests/tutorial.test.ts), and for a night begun in the past, with nothing changed (tests/simulation.test.ts). Until 2026-10-13 this said no test slept through a commitment with life.sleep and checked it missed, or read the morning’s notice: the guide’s worked examples slept through classes, orientation and partner rehearsals by then (tests/guide-examples-school.test.ts, tests/guide-examples-coursework.test.ts), and since then a plan slept through is missed and named in the notice once, across a reload (tests/sleep-commitments.test.ts). The review of 2026-10-13 found two defects, both fixed that day and held there: the notice named a commitment kept between the booking and the bedtime, and a bedtime inside a commitment still to come was taken and the commitment counted kept; it’s refused now, the save left as it was. Readiness is read after nights slept through the command, but between lives that sleep the same and differ in their workouts (tests/looking-after.test.ts, tests/wellbeing-bites.test.ts), not between nights. docs/GAMEPLAY-COVERAGE.md calls life.sleep partial for the same gap. capabilities.limits: Until 2026-10-12 this was called Verified, while two of its claims had no test through the command, and until later that day these limits called a shower, an hour unwinding and a meal you needed checked through the command, while the shower and the meal were checked on applyLookingAfter called directly and nothing that reads an hour unwound was checked. Driven through life.look_after and checked: a meal feeds, and leaves readiness above the same afternoon without one, and lifts a spender’s mood more (tests/looking-after.test.ts, tests/traits-connected.test.ts); a meal does what its line said, and one that can’t be done goes last with the command’s own refusal (tests/look-after.test.ts); a meal the bank can’t pay is refused and takes nothing (tests/defects-g4-1.test.ts); an hour unwinding takes off more stress than an hour going by and lifts the mood, and eight weeks of workouts build fitness, and with it condition and readiness, against a twin who didn’t (tests/looking-after.test.ts). What isn’t: that a meal you needed lifts the mood more, a shower’s hygiene and stress, a workout’s cost in energy and how much unwinding helps a person are checked on applyLookingAfter called directly (tests/looking-after.test.ts), and tests/wellbeing-bites.test.ts issues a shower among four actions a day and can’t tell its part. No test checks the hunger toll a meal spares, on condition and the mood; what reads a shower, readiness’s hygiene factor and the grimy hours’ toll on the mood; or what reads the stress an hour unwinding takes off: readiness, the night’s sleep and catching the flu. A meal is offered and refused in spend’s own words for every way of paying, and refused before its hour (tests/defects-r1-1.test.ts), and one eaten or ordered in at 11:40 PM is bought through the command and paid as it’s ordered, at delivery’s price for one ordered in, and feeds (tests/defects-r3a-1.test.ts); until 2026-10-12 no test ordered in through the command, and this said so. The weight a meal eaten out adds isn’t checked there: eatsOut and bodyDay are called directly (tests/body.test.ts); the order’s menu line is refused when it can’t be afforded (tests/defects-g4-1.test.ts). And no workout through the command checks an injury: mayHurt is called directly (tests/injury.test.ts, tests/life-fixes.test.ts), and the long runs skip a workout while hurt rather than check one. docs/GAMEPLAY-COVERAGE.md called life.look_after:eat, life.look_after:order, life.look_after:wash, life.look_after:exercise and life.look_after:unwind partial for these gaps when this was written; each has been verified since the evidence rounds of 2026-10-13, and what each now checks through the command is said in its row there, not here. From 2026-10-16 (brief 09) the command itself has a row too, life.look_after: an action not on the menu refused with nothing changed, what it returns as changed, an action id lived once, and a meal’s payment refused after its refusal passed, a guard no play reaches, held on a test double (tests/remaining-09-coverage.test.ts, tests/remaining-09-coverage-guard.test.ts). No test reloads a save between looking after and its effect. A bath, a swim, sitting outside, the laundry and cleaning went with the home on 2026-10-09

capabilities.goal: Put your own plans on the calendar, call them off or skip them, and set how fast the clock runs
capabilities.entry: Calendar: a day, Put Something On It; an entry’s Call It Off. Top bar: when a plan comes due, Skip It or Go; the clock’s speed
capabilities.preconditions: A plan passes checkPlan (a title, a start, a length from half an hour to all day, in the town you’re in); calling off only before it starts, skipping only once it’s due
capabilities.effects: A plan holds the time and halts the clock when it comes due. Skipped, it’s marked missed and costs nothing but the plan; called off, it comes off the calendar. The speed is paused or live, and nothing else is a preference. Until 2026-10-12 this said paused, live, fast or faster: the command took ‘fast’ and ‘faster’, which no control sent, and refuses them since (world/world.ts), and a save that stored one opens at live (migrate, src/engine/index.ts)
capabilities.persists: universe.scheduled (the plan’s item and status), universe.preferences.timeSpeed
readers: occupiedAt (systems/life.ts), which refuses sleep, looking after, coursework, play reading and production work while a plan runs

the clock’s halt at a due item (advanceTo and advanceBy with stopOnPlayerRequired, core/simulation.ts), held as standingAt (app/game-context.tsx) and put on screen with Skip It or Go (ui/shell/TimeControls.tsx)
the live clock’s rate, SPEED_MULTIPLIER (app/game-context.tsx)
capabilities.provenance: SLATE’s estimate
capabilities.limits: Until 2026-10-12 this was called Verified, while two of its commands were checked for their change alone, and it named the live clock’s rate as read in ui/shell/TimeControls.tsx, where it’s SPEED_MULTIPLIER in app/game-context.tsx.
